title: Stage 2: A teammate got there first
summary: 11:30. Priya pushed a change to the same lines in Cart.cs. Your push is rejected; integrate her work and resolve the conflict.

steps.title: Briefing
body: You polished the coupon logic and committed again. Meanwhile Priya merged *Free shipping over 50* into `main`, touching the same `Total()` method in `Cart.cs`.
You want your branch on top of her work before review. Your team rebases feature branches.

steps.prompt: You run `git fetch` and then `git status` on your branch, whose upstream is `origin/main` for this check. What is the second line? (One line.)
steps.answer: Your branch and 'origin/main' have diverged, and have 2 and 1 different commits each, respectively.
steps.explain: C1 and C2 are yours only; P is Priya's only.
accept:
Your branch and 'origin/main' have diverged,
and have 2 and 1 different commits each, respectively.

steps.prompt: You run `git rebase origin/main`. C1 replays cleanly; C2 conflicts in `Cart.cs`. In the conflict markers during a **rebase**, which side is `HEAD`?
options: The commits being built: Priya's P plus your already-replayed C1'; your C2 is the incoming side
steps.explain: During a rebase HEAD is the new history under construction. The commit being replayed (yours) is the *incoming* side. It feels reversed compared with merge, so read the labels.

steps.prompt: This is the conflicted region. The right answer keeps **both** behaviours: Priya's free-shipping line first, then your coupon line. Write the resolved lines exactly (no markers), keeping the indentation.
steps.explain: Neither side alone is right. Note the remaining question for the product owner: should free shipping be decided before or after the discount? The code above decides it before. Conflicts are often a design question in disguise.

steps.prompt: Arrange the rest of the rebase after editing `Cart.cs`.
steps.explain: Mark resolved, let the rebase finish, prove it works, then update your already-pushed branch safely. A plain `git push` would be rejected because the branch was rewritten.

steps.title: Resolve conflict markers
prompt: Write the core of a *take ours / take theirs / keep both* tool. `Resolve(List<string> lines, string choice)` removes every conflict block and keeps:
Lines outside conflict blocks are kept as they are. A block starts with a line beginning `<<<<<<< ` and ends with a line beginning `>>>>>>> `; the divider is exactly `=======`.
starter: static List<string> Resolve(List<string> lines, string choice)
solution: static List<string> Resolve(List<string> lines, string choice)
int state = 0; // 0 outside, 1 in ours, 2 in theirs
hints: Track a state: outside, inside ours, inside theirs.
Collect the two sides in separate lists, and decide what to emit when you reach the `>>>>>>>` line.
